raw_case_text:
An 82-year-old male was diagnosed with bronchial asthma at 10 years of age and treated with inhalants and he did not receive treatment for asthma since the age of 30 because of the resolution of bronchial asthma. He was followed at our hospital for idiopathic interstitial pneumonia by annual regular chest X-ray and computed tomography (CT) scans for 4 years. The patient's interstitial pneumonia, with minimal change in radiological findings was stable over the years, he complained no symptoms. He did not indicate exposure to fungus. Chest X-ray and CT scan obtained in December 2017 revealed high-attenuation mucus plug in right intermediate bronchial trunk, right pleural effusion (Fig. 1a), and infiltration in the right lung field (Fig. 1b). 
We also found unilateral bronchiectasis in the right upper lobe.
Additionally, a slight fibrotic change along the pleural line reflecting interstitial pneumonia was observed. CT of paranasal sinuses obtained to investigate nasal congestion for 3 years, revealed high-attenuation mucus plug in the left ethmoid sinuses (Fig. 2). Physical examination revealed decreased breath sounds in the right lower lung field. No wheezing and rhonchi were observed on auscultation. 
Blood tests showed a total leucocyte count of 9300/mm3 with 8% eosinophils (absolute eosinophil count, 744/mm3) and elevated C-reactive protein. Radioimmunosorbent test revealed elevated IgE levels (1460 IU/ml), and the radioimmunosorbent test for specific IgE antibodies against Aspergillus, Penicillium and Candida were positive. Serum precipitins to Aspergillus were also positive. We confirmed local urticaria and lash 15 min after subcutaneous injection of A. fumigatus antigen and this was positive of immediate cutaneous hypersensitivity reaction. He had a history of right nephrectomy because of renal cancer and did not experience recurrence.
Pulmonary function test showed the following: forced vital capacity (FVC), 1.86 L (55.4% of predicted value); forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1), 1.60 L (64.3% of predicted value); and FEV1/FVC, 86.0%. Bronchoscopy for definite diagnosis confirmed bronze-colored, hard mucus plug in the right intermediate bronchial trunk (Fig. 3a), and pathological examination of multiple biopsy specimens stained by hematoxylin-eosin revealed allergic mucin with layers of mucus, eosinophils, and eosinophil-predominant mixed inflammatory cell infiltrate and Charcot-Leyden crystals (Fig. 4a). Grocott's stain revealed fungal hyphae with a 45  branch angle within the allergic mucin (Fig. 4b). We performed open biopsy of the ethmoid sinuses and found similar mucus plug there, which revealed similar pathological findings in the right intermediate bronchial trunk (Fig. 3b), including fungal hyphae with a 45  branch angle within allergic mucin (Fig. 4c). Mucus plug cultures were positive for A. fumigatus. The patient met of the diagnostic criteria for ABPA by Rosenberg and Patterson as well as those for AFRS, and thus he was diagnosed with SAM syndrome.  
The patient was treated with 0.5 mg/kg prednisolone daily for 1 month, which was reduced to 0.35 mg/kg prednisolone daily. His total IgE levels fell to 206 IU/ml after 3 months. CT of the lung and paranasal sinuses showed apparent amelioration (Fig. 5a-c), and nasal congestion was resolved after 3 months steroid therapy. Now, there has been about 1 year and 4 months after the diagnosis, the patient is currently receiving oral steroid therapy (0.1 mg/kg) and remains in good condition with no deteriorations.

subjective.chief_complaint: An 82-year-old male with a 3-year history of chronic nasal congestion and a remote history of childhood asthma presented with asymptomatic right lung infiltrates, right pleural effusion, and central bronchial mucus plugging on annual surveillance chest imaging.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Followed annually by chest X-ray and CT for 4 years for stable, asymptomatic idiopathic interstitial pneumonia, the patient was found in December 2017 to have a new high-attenuation mucus plug in the right truncus intermedius, right upper lobe bronchiectasis, right lung infiltrates, and a right pleural effusion, alongside a 3-year history of chronic nasal congestion.
subjective.past_medical_history: Childhood bronchial asthma diagnosed at age 10 and in complete medication-free remission since age 30; stable idiopathic interstitial pneumonia followed for 4 years; prior right radical nephrectomy for renal cell carcinoma without recurrence; no known fungal exposure.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for chronic nasal congestion for 3 years; negative for cough, wheezing, or dyspnea.

objective.physical_examination: Chest auscultation revealed decreased breath sounds in the right lower lung field without wheezing or rhonchi.
objective.routine_investigations: Blood tests showed WBC 9,300/mm3 with mild eosinophilia (8% eosinophils, absolute eosinophil count 744/mm3), elevated CRP, and markedly elevated total serum IgE of 1,460 IU/mL (declining to 206 IU/mL after 3 months of prednisolone). RAST specific IgE antibodies were positive for Aspergillus, Penicillium, and Candida; serum precipitating antibodies to Aspergillus were positive; and subcutaneous skin testing with Aspergillus fumigatus antigen elicited an immediate wheal-and-flare reaction at 15 minutes. Spirometry showed FVC 1.86 L (55.4% predicted), FEV1 1.60 L (64.3% predicted), and FEV1/FVC 86.0%.
objective.advanced_workup: Chest CT (December 2017) demonstrated a high-attenuation mucus plug obstructing the right truncus intermedius, right upper lobe bronchiectasis, right parenchymal infiltration, right pleural effusion, and mild subpleural interstitial fibrosis. Paranasal sinus CT revealed a high-attenuation mucus plug in the left ethmoid sinus. Bronchoscopy confirmed a hard, bronze-colored mucus plug in the right truncus intermedius, and open left ethmoid sinus biopsy retrieved an identical mucus plug; histopathology (H&E and Grocott stains) of both the bronchial and ethmoid sinus specimens demonstrated laminated allergic mucin packed with eosinophils, Charcot-Leyden crystals, and 45-degree branching septate fungal hyphae, and cultures of the mucus plugs grew Aspergillus fumigatus.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Sinobronchial allergic mycosis (SAM) syndrome—comprising concurrent allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA, fulfilling Rosenberg-Patterson criteria) and left ethmoidal allergic fungal rhinosinusitis (AFRS)—caused by Aspergillus fumigatus in an 82-year-old man after a 52-year remission of childhood asthma, confirmed by high-attenuation sinobronchial mucus plugs on CT, peripheral eosinophilia, elevated total IgE (1,460 IU/mL), positive A. fumigatus skin test, specific IgE, and precipitins, and identical Grocott-positive 45-degree branching hyphae and A. fumigatus culture growth from both bronchial and ethmoid sinus allergic mucin. Treated with oral prednisolone (0.5 mg/kg/day for 1 month, tapered to 0.35 mg/kg/day and maintained at 0.1 mg/kg/day), achieving resolution of nasal congestion, reduction of total IgE to 206 IU/mL, and radiographic clearing of lung and sinus lesions at 3 and 16 months.
